query: FeCoNi is an fcc alloy with high saturation magnetization and a low coercive field. Earlier studies examined the high-entropy alloys FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, but both exhibited soft ferromagnetism. A qualifying high-entropy alloy must have an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R. Subject to these constraints, what single intervention could produce a FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with greater coercivity than the prior derivatives? Present one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an appropriate FeCoNi-based baseline, defines the conditions over which it should apply, cites supporting observations from earlier work, and proposes a discriminating experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of a refractory metal element, such as Ti, to the FeCoNi alloy will increase its coercivity by introducing lattice distortion and pinning domain walls, thus producing a high-entropy alloy with greater coercivity than the prior derivatives.
generation.material_initial_state: fcc alloy with high saturation magnetization and low coercive field
generation.intervention: addition of 5 at.% Ti to the FeCoNi alloy
generation.conditions: almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R
generation.structural_mediator: lattice distortion and domain wall pinning
generation.mechanism: the introduction of Ti will increase the lattice distortion, which will pin the domain walls and increase the coercivity of the alloy
generation.predicted_outcome: an increase in coercivity of at least 20% relative to the baseline FeCoNi alloy
generation.baseline: FeCoNi alloy with a coercivity of 100 Oe
generation.boundary: the addition of Ti will only be effective if the alloy maintains its fcc structure and the configurational entropy is above 1.0R
generation.uncertainty: the exact amount of Ti required to achieve the desired coercivity and the potential effects of other refractory metal elements on the alloy's properties

falsification_experiment.design: prepare a series of FeCoNiTi alloys with varying Ti content and measure their coercivity using a vibrating sample magnetometer
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: if the coercivity of the FeCoNiTi alloy with 5 at.% Ti is not at least 20% higher than the baseline FeCoNi alloy, the hypothesis is falsified
